section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the distinction between the revelation of the name Havayah to the Patriarchs and its revelation at the Giving of the Torah.
section.t: "And Elokim spoke to Moshe and said to him, 'I am Havayah. And I appeared to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yaakov... but My name Havayah I did not make known to them.'"
And the precise point
in this of the Baal HaHilula is known, regarding what is said, "but My name Havayah I did not make known to them,"
for is not the name Havayah stated many times in speech to the Patriarchs?
And as Rashi's commentary raised this difficulty.
Also, one must understand what is said here specifically, "I am Havayah,"
what is the connection of the name Havayah to the Exodus from Egypt and to the Giving of the Torah
(which are connected to each other,
as it is stated,
"When you take the people out of Egypt, you will serve Elokim on this mountain").
Now, from what is explained in this discourse in Torah Or,
it is understood
that to the Patriarchs, the name Havayah was revealed only through the name Elokim,
which in general is the aspect of the name Havayah below,
but the name Havayah above was not made known to them,
unlike at the Giving of the Torah, when the name Havayah that is above enclothing in the name Elokim was revealed,
the aspect of the name Havayah above.
Therefore, before the Giving of the Torah, there was a decree
that the upper ones would not descend to the lower ones and the lower ones would not ascend to the upper ones,
and at the Giving of the Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, nullified the decree and said that the lower ones will ascend to the upper ones,
and the upper ones will descend to the lower ones,
and I will begin,
as it is stated,
"And Havayah descended upon Mount Sinai,"
and it is written,
"And to Moshe He said, 'Ascend to Havayah.'"
And this is what is said to him here, "I am Havayah,"
that a new revelation begins,
that the name Havayah which is above enclothing in the name Elokim will be revealed,
the name Havayah above.
